anchors.1: Opening line could start any script. No tension.
anchors.3: Opening creates curiosity but doesn't demand attention.
anchors.5: Opening line makes a stranger stop scrolling.

anchors.1: A new viewer cannot tell what is happening.
anchors.3: A new viewer understands after 3-4 messages.
anchors.5: A new viewer knows exactly what is happening from the first message.

anchors.1: Generic lines. Any character could say any line.
anchors.3: Some specific details but falls back to generic roasts.
anchors.5: Every line has a specific detail that makes it feel like a real event.

anchors.1: Conflict stays flat. Same energy start to finish.
anchors.5: Each beat raises the stakes measurably. No regression.

anchors.1: Ending can be guessed from the hook.
anchors.5: Ending could not have been predicted. The final line changes how you read the whole thing.

anchors.3: Characters sound mostly distinct but share phrases.
anchors.5: Each character's lines could be attributed correctly with names removed.

anchors.1: NOTABOT could be replaced by any sarcastic character.
anchors.3: NOTABOT uses some of its mechanisms but feels generic.
anchors.5: NOTABOT's role, voice, and mechanism are all correct for this episode's designated role.

anchors.1: Multiple lines add nothing. Filler present.
anchors.3: 1-2 lines could be cut without losing anything.
anchors.5: Zero filler. Removing any line loses a beat or a setup.

anchors.1: Script trails off or ends mid-conflict.
anchors.5: Ending is a button — the last line is the best line and recontextualises the whole script.

anchors.1: Premise, hook, and shape all appear in the ledger.
anchors.3: Premise is fresh but shape and ending type repeat.
anchors.5: Premise, mechanism, and ending type have not appeared in the last 20 scripts.
